tagline: Chalawan's town, Bueng Si Fai, and riverside life along the Nan
introHtml: Phichit is a small, quiet town in the lower North that plenty of people drive straight past on the way up north — but stop in and you'll find a place with stories of its own. Locals are tied to the legend of Kraithong and Chalawan the crocodile, which has become the symbol of the province. Most visitors head to Bueng Si Fai, the big freshwater lake in the middle of town with a giant crocodile statue, pay respects to Luang Pho Phet at Wat Tha Luang, and walk the old town of Phichit where the moat and remnants of the wall still stand. The town sits along the Nan River, with the Tha Khoi pomelo orchards and an easygoing riverside farming life you can soak up without any rush.
bestTime: November–February, cool and pleasant — good for walking around town and Bueng Si Fai. Around the end of Buddhist Lent in September–October there's a long-boat racing festival at Wat Tha Luang.

highlights.name: Bueng Si Fai
highlights.blurb: A large freshwater lake in the middle of town with a giant statue of Chalawan the crocodile as its landmark. Easy place to stroll, cycle, and feed the fish.

highlights.name: Luang Pho Phet, Wat Tha Luang
highlights.blurb: The town's revered Buddha image that locals and visitors alike come to pay respects to. The temple sits by the Nan River in the center of town.

highlights.name: Legend of Kraithong and Chalawan
highlights.blurb: The tale of Chalawan the crocodile and Kraithong, tied to Phichit until it became a symbol you'll see all across the province.

highlights.name: Phichit Old Town Park
highlights.blurb: An ancient town zone where the moat, earthen walls, and old temples remain, set in shady woods. A quiet spot to wander and take photos.

highlights.name: Tha Khoi pomelo
highlights.blurb: Phichit's famous pomelo — sweet and juicy, grown around Tha Khoi sub-district. Buy some to eat or take home from the orchards and roadside stalls.

highlights.name: Long-boat racing at Wat Tha Luang
highlights.blurb: A long-boat racing tradition by the Nan River around the end of Buddhist Lent — a big annual event that draws people from across the province.

foodScene.name: Tha Khoi pomelo and fruit
foodScene.note: The town's signature pomelo is sweet and juicy, sold at orchards and roadside stalls. You'll also find seasonal fruit from the orchards along the Nan River.

foodScene.name: Old-school noodle shops
foodScene.note: In town there are several long-running noodle shops with round, mellow broth at local prices — an easy meal the locals go for.

foodScene.name: Isan food
foodScene.note: Som tam, grilled chicken, and laab are easy to find at shops around town and along the roads. Bold flavors that hit the spot for travelers.

foodScene.name: Mu kratha
foodScene.note: A popular dinner for Phichit locals, with plenty of places to choose from around town. Relaxed vibe and friendly prices.

foodScene.name: Freshwater fish and riverside food
foodScene.note: Phichit sits on the Nan River, so local restaurants serve freshwater fish dishes like grilled fish and tom yum fish.

foodScene.name: Evening markets and street food
foodScene.note: The town markets and walking street have evening eats — rice-and-curry plates, fried snacks, and local sweets to graze on.

foodScene.name: Cafes in town
foodScene.note: Small cafes have opened in town and by Bueng Si Fai — a spot to sip coffee after a day of wandering.

foodScene.name: Local sweets and souvenirs
foodScene.note: Shops in town carry local sweets and souvenirs to take home, beyond the province's signature pomelo.

attractions.name: Bueng Si Fai
attractions.blurb: A big freshwater lake in the middle of town with the Chalawan crocodile statue. Stroll, cycle, feed the fish, and catch the sunset over the water.

attractions.name: Wat Tha Luang
attractions.blurb: A temple by the Nan River in the center of town, home to Luang Pho Phet, the revered Buddha image people come to pay respects to.

attractions.name: Phichit Old Town Park
attractions.blurb: An ancient town zone where the moat, earthen walls, the old Wat Mahathat, and the city pillar shrine remain, set in shady woods. A quiet place to wander.

attractions.name: Wat Pho Prathap Chang
attractions.blurb: An old temple believed to be the birthplace of King Suriyenthrathibodi (Sanphet VIII), with an ancient-style ordination hall and surrounding walls.

attractions.name: Chalawan Cave
attractions.blurb: A spot tied to the legend of Chalawan the crocodile, with a shrine and crocodile statue — a stop for anyone wanting to trace the town's legend.

attractions.name: Wat Khao Rup Chang
attractions.blurb: A temple on a low hill with a chedi and a viewpoint over Phichit town. Worth climbing up to pay respects and take photos.

attractions.name: Tha Khoi pomelo orchards
attractions.blurb: Pomelo orchards along the Nan River where you can see the farming life and taste pomelo fresh off the tree. A good stop to grab souvenirs to take home.

attractions.name: Markets and the Nan riverfront in town
attractions.blurb: The riverside town district along the Nan, with markets, restaurants, and cafes to wander and catch the cool breeze after seeing the sights.
